newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast jet fuel prices drawing imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast jet fuel prices drawing imports.

text.p: Strong prices for U.S. West Coast jet fuel will draw a steady stream of Gulf Coast shipments to California this month, traders said on Friday.
The first of four cargoes will arrive later next week, traders said, noting each shipment contains 200,000 to 300,000 barrels. Thereafter, one will arrive every week for the rest of the month.

Although arbitrage, or price appeal, of jet fuel has shifted from California to New York this week, demand here remains brisk, with buyers lined up to take the first two shipments, market observers said.
"These were cargoes committed a while ago," a trader said.

Jet fuel supply in PADD 5 West Coast remains relatively low, with 6.7 million barrels in storage for the week ended January 24, a 1.3 million drop from the previous week, and 1.2 million barrels below year-ago levels.

And with Los Angeles CARB diesel prices up nine percent this week to 87 cents a gallon, refiners will likely cut jet output in favor of diesel, tightening a supply already hit by maintenance and equipment failure outages at plants, and strong demand from airlines, traders said.
"The West Coast will probably be able to absorb jet because people will be sacrificing jet for CARB diesel," a trader said.
Manufactures of diesel and jet fuel use the same processing units for both products, alternating output in accordance with market pressures.

Spot prices for jet ranged 81 to 82.50 cents late Thursday, slightly higher than mid-week levels. But traders saw prices relaxing after the cargoes arrive. Already, spot prices have become backwardated, reflection gradual weakness.
"The West Coast front supplies are worth a lot more than distant ones," a trader said.
